items.fullText: 산업 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 이재용의 원픽…"될 사람이 됐다" 엔비디아 뚫은 30년 삼성맨 [강경주의 테크X] 입력 2026.11.21 09:30 수정 2026.11.21 09:40 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 강경주 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. <테크X131> 황상준 삼성전자 신임 사장은 누구 D램 설계부터 마케팅까지 반도체 개발·사업 경험 두루 갖춰 PIM·CXL 주목…데이터 병목 해결 기술 제시 "기술 혁신 중심엔 삼성"…메모리 초격차 자신감 황상준 신임 삼성전자 메모리사업부장 사장 / 사진=삼성전자 삼성전자 가 고대역폭메모리(HBM) 주도권 탈환의 선봉에 선 황상준 메모리개발담당 겸 D램개발실장 부사장을 메모리사업부장(사장)으로 승진시켰다. 삼성전자 내부에선 "될 사람이 됐다"는 평가가 나왔다. 관련 업계 안팎에선 차세대 HBM과 D램의 설계·공정 경쟁력을 한 단계 끌어올리고, 메모리 기술의 근본적인 혁신을 주도할 적임자라고 평가했다. 1996년 입사한 정통 삼성…30년 만에 메모리 수장 1996년 입사한 정통 삼성…30년 만에 메모리 수장21일 반도체 업계에 따르면 삼성전자는 전날 사장 승진 3명, 보직 변경 3명 등 총 6명의 '2027년 정기 사장단' 인사를 발표했다. 승진자는 모두 역대급 실적을 낸 반도체 부문에서 나왔다. 업계에서는 메모리사업부장에 오른 황 신임 사장을 주목해야 한다고 입을 모은다. 황 사장을 두고 내부에서는 "예상한 인사"라는 반응이다. 신입사원으로 입사해 30년간 삼성전자에서 일한 개발자가 메모리 사업 전체를 책임지게 됐다. 1972년생인 황 사장은 고려대 전기공학과를 졸업하고 같은 대학에서 석사학위를 받은 뒤 1996년 2월 삼성전자에 입사했다. 2008년에는 고려대 반도체공학 박사학위를 취득했다. 삼성전자 입사 후 2017년 11월까지 21년 넘게 메모리사업부 D램개발실 D램설계팀에서 경력을 쌓은 그는 이후 플래시개발실 플래시설계팀장을 맡아 낸드플래시로 개발 경험을 확장했다. 2020년에는 전략마케팅실 상품기획팀장을 거쳐 D램설계팀장으로 복귀했다. 2022년 말 마케팅팀장을, 2023년 7월 D램개발실장에 올랐다. 제품을 설계하는 기술뿐 아니라 고객이 요구하는 성능과 시장 수요를 함께 경험한 그는 지난해 12월부터는 메모리개발담당과 D램개발실장을 겸임하며 메모리 제품 전반의 개발을 총괄했다. 개발 현장에서 출발해 설계와 상품기획, 마케팅, 개발 총괄을 거쳐 사업부장에 오른 것이다. 황 사장이 D램개발실을 이끈 당시는 삼성전자가 HBM 시장에서 경쟁력 회복에 전사적인 역량을 쏟은 시기다. SK하이닉스 에 시장 주도권을 내주고 주요 고객사 공급이 지연되면서 삼성 메모리의 기술 경쟁력에 대한 우려가 커졌다. 이재용 삼성전자 회장이 결단을 내린 2024년 5월 전영현 부회장이 DS부문장으로 부임한 뒤 삼성전자는 HBM 개발 역량을 집중하며 반등을 꾀했다. 황 사장은 D램개발실장으로서 이 과정에 참여했고, 내부에서는 HBM3E 개선과 차세대 HBM4 개발을 이끈 공로를 높이 평가한 것으로 전해졌다. 특히 전 부회장이 신임하는 것으로 알려졌다. 지난해 말에는 별도로 운영하던 HBM개발팀이 D램개발실 산하로 재편됐고, 황 사장은 메모리개발담당까지 맡으며 역할을 넓혔다. 이번에는 전 부회장이 겸임하던 메모리사업부장을 넘겨받았다. 내부에서는 승진 가능성이 높았던 인사가 실제 사업부장에 오르자 축하와 기대가 이어지는 분위기다. 황 사장은 개발자는 기술과 결과로 평가받아야 한다는 원칙을 중시하는 인물이라는 평가를 받는다. 삼성전자는 "황 사장이 D램과 HBM 등 메모리 전 제품의 개발 경쟁력 확보를 주도했다"며 &

items.t: Markets plummet as tech sell-off intensifies
items.d: The stock market plummeted as a tech sell-off intensified after Anthropic's record-setting IPO. Nvidia also dragged markets lower, tumbling about 14% following a Reuters report that regulators are looking into accounting irregularities at the chip giant.

items.t: 한국서 '젠슨 황 사태' 터지면…인력 부족에 처벌은 솜방망이 [털리는 대한민국]
items.fullText: 사회 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 한국서 '젠슨 황 사태' 터지면…인력 부족에 처벌은 솜방망이 [털리는 대한민국] 입력 2026.11.21 06:00 수정 2026.11.21 08:12 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 이정우 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. [털리는 대한민국(4·끝) 법 제도의 공백] 중수청, 정원 못 채우고 시설도 아직 미비 경찰, 안보 인력은 증원 없이 재배치로 메워 간첩죄 넓혔지만, 산업기술 적용 여부 모호 산업계 "처벌 수위 낮아 유출 계속 되풀이" 전문가 "새로운 법제로 산업스파이 규율해야" 사진=REUTERS 젠슨 황 전 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)의 외도 상대로 지목된 앨리스 황의 스파이 의혹을 계기로 국내에서도 산업스파이에 대한 경계심이 커지고 있다. 2024년 국가정보원의 대공 수사권이 폐지된 데 이어 올해 국군방첩사령부와 검찰이 해체되면서 기술 탈취 공작에 제대로 대응할 수 있겠느냐는 우려가 제기된다. 중대범죄수사청은 정원의 3분의 2만 채웠고, 경찰은 기존 인력을 재배치해 부족분을 메우고 있다. 적발하더라도 처벌 수위가 낮아 기술 유출을 억제하기 어렵고, 간첩죄 적용에도 한계가 있는 게 현실이다. 수사부터 처벌까지 대응 체계를 종합적으로 점검해야 한다는 목소리가 나온다. ◇ 중수청은 정원 미달, 경찰은 인력 재배치 기사 내용과는 무관한 사진 /사진=연합뉴스 21일 정치권에 따르면 현행법상 민간인 대상 대공 수사를 할 수 있는 기관은 경찰과 중대범죄수사청뿐이다. 다만 중수청은 정원도 채우지 못한 상태다. 국회 행정안전위원회 예산안 검토보고서에 따르면 지난달 16일 기준 중수청 현원은 1901명으로 정원(2874명)의 66% 수준에 불과하다. 김지용 중수청장은 지난 10일 국무회의에서 "내년 2월 정도면 어느 정도 충원될 것으로 예상하고 있다"고 밝혔다. 김 청장은 중수청의 시설·장비와 업무공간에 대해 "12월 중순 정도에 완비될 것"이라고 했다. 중대범죄를 수사할 기본적인 여건도 아직 갖춰지지 않은 것이다. 이런 가운데 지난달 2일 개청 이후 같은 달 30일까지 전국 중수청의 사건 송치는 3건, 피의자 구속은 5건에 그쳤다. 중수청이 인력 보강과 시설 확충을 마치고 자리를 잡기 전까지 경찰의 안보수사 부담은 이어질 것으로 보인다. 사진=ChatGPT로 생성한 이미지 그러나 경찰도 인력 사정이 넉넉하지 않다. 안보경찰 인력 총원은 2024년 2307명에서 올해 9월 말 2300여명으로 소폭 감소하는 추세를 보이고 있다. 이에 대해 경찰청 관계자는 "수사 인력은 내부 인력 재배치를 통해 계속 보강하고 있다"고 설명했다. 실제 경찰은 지난 8월 산업기술 유출 범죄 수사를 전담할 인력 79명을 배치했다. 올해 초에는 전국 시도경찰청의 방첩 수사관을 41명 늘렸다. 다만 이는 전체 안보수사 총원을 늘리기보다 탈북민 신변 보호 등 수요가 줄어든 분야의 인력을 옮겨 부족분을 메우는 방식으로 이뤄졌다. 이 관계자는 행정안전부 측에 매년 증원을 요청하지만 잘 받아들여지지 않는다고 했다. 이어 "국가 안보는 직접 와닿지 않는 부분이다 보니 행안부의 인력 배치 우선순위에서 밀릴 수는 있다"면서도 "체감하기로는 인력이 너무 부족한 상황"이라고 토로했다. 자체적인 해외 정보 확보에도 제약이 있다. 현재 해외 대공 수사 전담 경찰 인력이 없다. 경찰청은 해외에서 직접 경찰 활동을 하는 데는 해당국의 주권 문제가 걸려 있어 국정원이 수집한 정보에 의존하고 있다고 했다. 내부적으로는 해외 파견 경찰 주재관 활용 등 자체 역량을 키우는 방안을 검토하고 있지만 현재로서는 한계가 있다고 밝혔다. ◇ "처벌 낮아 유출 되풀이"…간첩죄 적용도

items.t: 젠슨 황은 미녀 스파이에 낚인 게 아니다
Wall Street Reels as AI Fears Erupt; Nasdaq 100 Near Bear Market
items.d: Wall Street reeled on Friday as nagging concerns about the AI trade, which propelled US stocks from one high to the next for much of the year, turned into a full-blown, market-wide selloff. Anthropic PBC slumped after soaring in its public-market debut, while Nvidia Corp. sank 14%, pushing the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market.

items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab Build and test scientific applications by connecting up to four NVIDIA DGX Spark systems for a combined 512GB of shared memory, without waiting for a spot on shared systems. November 16, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. items.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors

items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w

items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Contribution and New AI Infrastructure At KubeCon, NVIDIA is putting tools to secure agents and run AI on Kubernetes in the hands of the cloud-native community. November 10, 2026 by Warren Barkley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future.
